title: Backflow preventer leaking from the vent: do not plug the discharge
description: Use the device family, exact opening, flow severity, timing, pressure events, and freeze history to choose the safe next route.
prompt: How is the vent or relief opening discharging?
answer: An RPZ relief valve and a PVB air inlet are different mechanisms. Continuous discharge can reflect debris, pressure conditions, failed internals, or damage and needs the correct device-specific service.
urgency: Never cap, plug, pipe shut, or obstruct a relief or air opening. Protect people and property from flooding, spray, and ice.
diagramAlt: Backflow preventer with relief vent discharge path and observation points
identifiers: RPZ relief discharge exits below the zone between two checks.
PVB venting exits around the raised bonnet or air inlet.
A crack or fitting leak is not the same as intentional discharge geometry.

choices.label: Continuous flow from an RPZ relief opening
choices.detail: Internal fouling, pressure relationship, or component failure is possible.

choices.label: Water from the top of a PVB
choices.detail: Use the PVB timing and freeze path.

choices.label: A brief release after a pressure event
choices.detail: Record duration and recurrence; do not assume normal or failed yet.

steps.title: Identify the assembly
steps.body: Use the full body shape, test cocks, bonnet, relief location, and model label.

steps.title: Record the event
steps.body: Capture severity, duration, pressure changes, valve work, and weather.

steps.title: Close the compliance loop
steps.body: Repair or replacement may require a passing retest and accepted report.

safeChecks: Move vulnerable property away from discharge if safe.
Record the model and exact exit point.
notThisDevice: A threaded fitting leak follows a different repair path.
A pressure regulator bell leak is not a backflow relief event.
A sewer backwater valve does not discharge potable supply water.
evidenceNote: The page distinguishes observable device geometry and urgency. Only a qualified test and manufacturer procedure can confirm the failed component.
